construct: cEnc ΔCyt lacking the N-terminal diheme cytochrome domain
condition:
recombinant engineered cEnc ΔCyt expressed anaerobically in E. coli BL21(DE3) Sta
r; predicted signal peptide and N-terminal diheme cytochrome domain removed; cargo-free shell characterization
notes:
Structurally distinct engineered ΔCyt assembly. Removal of the N-terminal diheme cytochrome domain produced stable 
~29 nm capsids compared with 33 nm WT cEnc, showing that the native fusion domain influences global shell size. The study reports ~15 co-purifying NIR copies per 180-mer ΔCyt capsid when the isolated NIR cargo domain was coexpressed; 180 shell subunits are therefore recorded and T=3 is inferred from the 180-mer icosahedral architecture. The isolated NIR-loaded condition is not treated as a separate assembly because full-length NIR-HAO was insoluble and no distinct cage architecture was demonstrated.
shell_sequence_change: Removal of the N-terminal diheme cytochrome domain (ΔCyt).
shell_change_alignment_note: Native 277-aa retained segment aligns to reference residues 87–363; residues 1–86 absent. Full experimental plasmid DNA not independently verified.
